Q: Wrong characters from PDF when extracting text using PDF Pig in c# A:

You could write your own decoder but need to map the characters to a known pattern so you need more than that short sample here is a map of what you have given so far.

The grid maps PDF UTF16 Binary "TOKENS" (Character IDs) to a place in the Unicode grid. It is rudimentary and there are better commercial tools but it allows to see WHY a font CMAP looks like "MojiBake".

For your convenience the CSV format Character MAP file is temporarily available (click the download button top right of this page.) at https://github.com/GitHubRulesOK/HoldingBay/blob/main/veridian-ANSI.csv

the 11 Kb Winform32bit exe (Use import first then add your own remap values and save as new CSV) is also at https://github.com/GitHubRulesOK/HoldingBay/blob/main/remapper256.exe

Once you Understand the array logic you can code around that font in that document.

Q: scipy.optimize.minimize for scipy.integrate.solve_ivp results in "success: False" A:

Your estimate is (way) out to lunch.

The default method of minimize does not do well on this problem. SLSQP does better. Not all optimizers are made equal.

If unmodified, the Jacobian is 0 for your second variable due to its huge scale. Take the log.

You're forcing the IVP routine to a low resolution. Let it take a higher (auto-determined) resolution by reducing the tolerance.

import functools
import typing

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
from scipy.optimize import minimize


type FloatOrArray = float | np.ndarray

class FInterp(typing.Protocol):
    def __call__[T: FloatOrArray](self, x: T) -> T:
        ...

class SolveB(typing.Protocol):
    def __call__(self, r: float, K: float) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        ...


def spm(
    t: float, B_flat: np.ndarray, r: float, K: float, f_func: FInterp,
) -> float:
    """
    Schaefer Population Model
    t: time
    B: biomass
    r: growth rate
    K: carrying capacity
    f_func: interpolation function for F
    """
    B, = B_flat
    F = f_func(t)
    dBdt = B*(r*(1 - B/K) - F)
    return dBdt


def objective(params: np.ndarray, B_func: FInterp, solve_b: SolveB) -> float:
    r, logK = params
    te, Be = solve_b(r, np.exp(logK))
    err = (Be - B_func(te))/te.size
    return err.dot(err)  # sum of squares


def solve(biomass_obs: np.ndarray, years: np.ndarray, f_obs: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float]:
    r0 = 0.15
    K0 = 1e6
    initial_guess = r0, np.log(K0)

    curried = functools.partial(
        solve_ivp, fun=spm, t_span=years[[0, -1]], y0=biomass_obs[:1], method='LSODA',
        rtol=1e-4)
    f_func = functools.partial(np.interp, xp=years, fp=f_obs)
    B_func = functools.partial(np.interp, xp=years, fp=biomass_obs)

    def solve_b(r: float, K: float) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        sol = curried(args=(r, K, f_func))
        if not sol.success:
            raise ValueError(sol.message)
        return sol.t, sol.y[0]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.scatter(years, biomass_obs, label='data')
    ax.plot(*solve_b(r0, K0), label='estimate')

    result = minimize(method='slsqp', fun=objective, x0=initial_guess, args=(B_func, solve_b))
    print(result.message)
    r, logK = result.x
    K = np.exp(logK)
    ax.plot(*solve_b(r, K), label='fit')
    ax.legend()
    plt.show()
    return r, K


def main() -> None:
    biomass_obs = np.array((7049, 6536, 5886, 5585, 5826))
    years = np.array((1961, 1962, 1963, 1964, 1965))
    f_obs = np.array((0.22, 0.269, 0.227, 0.135, 0.129))
    r, K = solve(biomass_obs, years, f_obs)
    print(f'r~{r:.4f} K~{K:.0f}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Optimization terminated successfully
r~0.1540 K~2441603

But a similar fit is achieved with r=0.1625, K=106543. This shows that tiny changes in r account for enormous changes in K.

Q: raise an exception in jinja if we passed in a variable that is not present in the template A:

To answer the actual question, how to detect extraneous variables and complain if there is any:

  1. Get all variables used by the template

    from jinja2 import Environment, PackageLoader, meta
env = Environment(loader=PackageLoader('gummi', 'templates'))
template_source = env.loader.get_source(env, 'page_content.html')
parsed_content = env.parse(template_source)
variables_used_by_template = meta.find_undeclared_variables(parsed_content)

    (credit: How to get list of all variables in jinja 2 templates)

  2. Compare this with the list of passed parameters, and check what are the extraneous ones. Something like this should work

    extraneous_variables = set(params.keys()) - set(variables_used_by_template)

Q: jasypt interferes with server startup logging and AbstractFailureAnalyzer in Spring Boot project A:

I met the same problem too. I had multiple profiles with slightly different logback configurations using logback-spring.xml And I found Jasypt somehow corrupts those configurations, with different phenomena. Sometimes, it prints CONSOLE (in my case, any profile has this phenomena) even asked not to. and sometimes, it does not log into FILE (in my case, only prod profile and duijie log into FILE). So as you can see, it is totally corrupted. The way I solve it is by adding -Dlogging.config=resources/logback-spring.xml in JVM paramter. And logging.config in any spring configuration like application.yml, application-local.yml or bootstrap.yml (spring cloud) will not function well. Or, it is said configure Jasypt in Java class not in application.yml will also have log function well.
